test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: For the implementation of which of the following did the Central Government estimate a total requirement of ₹2.31 lakh crore over a five year period from 2010-11 to 2014-15?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Education Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Education (RTE) Act**, enacted in **2009**, provides free and compulsory education to children aged **6 to 14 years** under **Article 21A** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Central Government estimated a total financial requirement of **₹2.31 lakh crore** over a **five-year period** (2010-11 to 2014-15) for implementing the provisions of the RTE Act.
 
• The act emphasizes on ensuring that no child is denied education due to financial constraints and mandates that private schools reserve **25% of their seats** for children from economically weaker sections.
 
• It promotes the establishment of neighborhood schools and the removal of barriers such as discrimination and lack of access, thus ensuring inclusive education for all.
 
• The RTE Act also includes provisions for infrastructure development in schools, teacher training, and quality education standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Education Act:**

 
 
• The **RTE Act** is a significant milestone in Indian education policy, ensuring free and compulsory education to children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• The act mandates schools to meet specific infrastructure standards, including classrooms, toilets, drinking water, and playgrounds.
 
• It also specifies pupil-teacher ratios to ensure quality education and better learning outcomes for students.
 
• The act prohibits physical punishment, mental harassment, and discrimination based on caste, gender, or disability.
 
• It encourages active participation of parents, community members, and local authorities in school management through School Management Committees (SMCs).
 
 
 
• **Ayushman Bharat Scheme:**
 
 
• Launched in **2018**, Ayushman Bharat aims to provide health insurance coverage of **₹5 lakh per family per year** for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• It is targeted at **economically vulnerable families** and supports the goal of universal health coverage.
 
• This scheme is not directly related to education but addresses healthcare needs.
 
 
 
• **Right to Information Act:**
 
 
• The **Right to Information (RTI) Act**, enacted in **2005**, empowers citizens to seek information from public authorities, ensuring transparency and accountability in governance.
 
• It is not linked to the financial allocation mentioned in the question as it pertains to governance rather than education.
 
 
 
• **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA):**
 
 
• Initiated in **2001**, SSA focuses on universalizing elementary education by providing access to schools, improving infrastructure, and ensuring teacher availability.
 
• While related to education, the financial allocation in question specifically pertains to the **RTE Act**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Framework:**

 
 
• The **Right to Education Act** falls under **Article 21A** of the Indian Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children.
 
• This act has significantly contributed to reducing dropout rates and increasing enrollment in schools across India.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of inclusive education by mandating the inclusion of children from marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Allocations:**
 
 
• The financial requirements for implementing the RTE Act were shared between the **Central and State Governments**, ensuring adequate resources for schools.
 
• The allocation highlights the government's focus on improving access to education and infrastructure development for schools.
